sources.entry: Python: _SlowTorch: Implementation of PyTorch from the ground up in 100% pure Python_

summary.one_liner: SlowTorch is a pure-Python reimplementation of core PyTorch tensor operations and reverse-mode automatic differentiation, built for learning how tensors and backpropagation work.
summary.what_it_does: The library provides a Tensor class with creation functions such as tensor, zeros, ones, full, arange, linspace, cat, and triangular helpers, plus arithmetic and comparison operations with broadcasting. It includes an autograd system: setting requires_grad=True records operations, and calling backward() fills in .grad values. Many operations have named backward nodes (for example AddBackward0, MulBackward0, MatmulBackward-style DotBackward0, SumBackward0, and activations such as ReLU, Tanh, Sigmoid, and Softmax). A render() method prints the computation graph. A small nn module offers Module, Linear, activation layers, and MSELoss/L1Loss, and optim.SGD is shown training a model. The README states it is not a replacement for PyTorch.
use_cases: learn how tensors and autograd work
experiment with a minimal neural network training loop
how_to_run: pip install -U git+ (latest version from the project's git repository; URL truncated in the README)
a = slowtorch.rand(2, 4, requires_grad=True); d = (a + b) * c; d.backward()
notable: Implements reverse-mode autodiff in pure Python, modeled on PyTorch's autograd and inspired by Karpathy's micrograd
Named backward functions (e.g. AddBackward0, MulBackward0) mirror PyTorch's grad_fn names
Custom render() method prints the computation graph of a tensor
Includes a small nn module and SGD optimizer that train a 5-layer tanh network in the README demo
Zero dependencies, so it is easy to read and modify
caveats: The README says it is not a replacement for PyTorch and should not be used as one
Pure Python makes it slow, as the name and README indicate
Requires Python 3.10 or newer; the author says it may not work on 3.9 and below due to typing changes
